title: Customer health, operations and cost alignment - handoff
summary: Monthly health check focused on usage trends, emergent latency spikes during peak routing, cost mitigation levers, and next-phase pilot for dedicated capacity. Agreed to run a short A/B synthetic benchmark of 1M tokens over two model profiles, share security docs, and schedule a deep-dive on SSO/KMS integrations next week.
topics: latency spikes and tail latency debugging
action_items: Jordan Lee: send per-route token breakdown and suggested batching config by 2026-06-14
Priya Nandy: prepare lightweight benchmark harness + instructions for A/B on 2 model variants by 2026-06-16
Marta Gonzalez: share SOC 2 / ISO slide deck and KMS integration notes by 2026-06-12
Evan Chu: provide 3 representative prompt flows and peak window times by 2026-06-13
Markus Huber: confirm network egress and VPC peering constraints by 2026-06-15
next_steps: Run A/B bench (hosted vs dedicated profile) week of 6/16
Redwood to send pricing scenarios for 3 committed levels and burst policy examples
Schedule SSO/KMS technical deep-dive (60m) with ParcelShift infra team - proposed 2026-06-17
Customer to confirm success criteria for 90-day pilot (latency p95 target, cost per 1k tokens)
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-10 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom | Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandy (Redwood SE), Marta Gonzalez (Redwood CSM), Evan Chu (ParcelShift Head of ML), Sofia Reyes (ParcelShift VP Product), Markus Huber (ParcelShift Infra), Amira Patel (ParcelShift Finance), Liam O'Connor (ParcelShift SRE)
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:08] Evan Chu: Yep, loud and clear. Sorry team I was in a routing standup right before this so jumping straight in.

[00:15] Jordan Lee: No worries. Agenda today: usage & cost trends, a couple of latency incidents from last fortnight, and then propose next steps around pilot economics and security handoff. Marta will kick us off with the adoption signal baseline.

[00:32] Marta Gonzalez: Thanks. ParcelShift adoption looks healthy; monthly token volume up ~18% month-over-month. But we saw a notable spike on 6/02 during peak routing—p95 jumped from 220ms to about 860ms on a handful of routes.
[00:50] Sofia Reyes: That spike corresponded with our Live ETA feature rollout, yes. We pushed heavier context and longer prompt histories which I think bloated seq length, maybe KV cache thrash?

[01:07] Priya Nandy: Right, longer context increases KV cache pressure. Also if the runtime kernel selection hit a less-optimized path for those sequence lengths you can see tail latency blow up. We suspect batching alignment and prefix cache misses contributed.

[01:28] Liam O'Connor: To add, our engineers saw more CPU churn on the routing service at that window, which pushed queuing into Redwood requests, exacerbating token latency — somewhat of a cascading overload.

[01:45] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. Two immediate levers: reduce sequence length via prompt trimming or structured prompts; and enable prefix caching for stable conversation flows. We can also recommend quantization profiles if quality is acceptable to reduce GPU time/cost.

[02:05] Amira Patel: On cost — we actually saw a 27% increase in spend tied exactly to that week. Finance flagged it because it pushed us over a projected monthly burn threshold. We need guardrails so spikes don't blow the budget.

[02:22] Jordan Lee: Understood. We typically propose a burst policy plus per-route rate limits and token caps; also cost alerts and token quotas for critical endpoints. We'll include a few pricing scenarios for committed capacity that smooths unit price for predictable spend.
[02:40] Evan Chu: Quick question: how much of that cost could be mitigated by caching vs moving to Dedicated? We're trying to reason tradeoffs — latency, predictability, and unit cost.

[02:56] Priya Nandy: Short answer: caching + batching can give you immediate per-token cost reduction while keeping hosted. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better p95 control during peak, but requires a commitment. For the specific workload pattern you shared, a hybrid approach (hosted with policy-based routing to dedicated for peak windows) often wins.
[03:20] Markus Huber: Would that hybrid routing be automatic? We can't have manual toggles in the middle of a production surge.

[03:28] Priya Nandy: Yes, you can set routing policies by time-of-day, traffic percentiles, or by token length. The runtime can fallback to hosted if dedicated is saturating. We can show the config example in the pilot package.
[03:45] Sofia Reyes: On security — our compliance team needs to see SOC 2 evidence and KMS key lifecycle docs. Also SSO integration is a blocker for our internal auditors.

[03:58] Marta Gonzalez: We'll share our SOC 2 report and an integration guide for external KMS (we support customer-managed keys and HSM flows). I'll send docs after the call. Also we have an SAML SSO guide and example metadata for IdP setup.
[04:15] Evan Chu: Great. For the pilot, we'll need a clear SLA and rollback plan if latency regresses. Can you detail fallbacks and how model rollouts are handled?

[04:30] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — rollouts are canary by default. You can define percentage splits and automatic rollback rules on quality or latency regressions. For SLAs, Dedicated includes uptime and latency SLOs; hosted is best-effort but we provide observability and automated fallback policies.
[04:50] Amira Patel: Pricing scenarios — can you show committed tiers for 100k, 500k, and 2M tokens/month with burst options? Also we want examples of worst-case invoice delta if a spike happens.
[05:07] Jordan Lee: We'll prepare three scenarios and a 'stress test' invoice projection, yes. Priya will include estimated savings from batching and quantization assumptions.
[05:20] Evan Chu: On the benchmarking A/B — can Redwood provide a harness that we can run from our infra? We prefer something reproducible rather than manual tests.

[05:33] Priya Nandy: We'll provide a lightweight harness (Python + curl examples) that runs synthetic prompt flows and measures p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. It will include instructions to run hosted profile vs a dedicated-like config. Expect a README and a sample script.

[05:50] Liam O'Connor: Network constraints: our VPC egress policy might limit peering options. Markus will validate whether ParcelShift can accept Redwood peering traffic or if we need a private deployment plan.
[06:05] Markus Huber: I'll check with infra; likely we can do VPC peering but may require exceptions. If not, private deployment could be an option but will extend timeline.
[06:20] Sofia Reyes: Timeline question — if we greenlight the pilot, how fast can we stand up a dedicated pool and start routing?

[06:28] Jordan Lee: Typical lead for dedicated reserved capacity is 2-4 weeks depending on region and commit. For a short-term proof we can simulate a dedicated profile on hosted (capacity tagging) so you get representative latency and unit costs sooner.
[06:45] Evan Chu: That would be good. We want to hit a p95 < 300ms for our core routing calls during peak within the pilot.

[06:54] Priya Nandy: Noted. We'll tune batching, kernel selection, and prefix cache settings to aim for that target in the A/B. Also we'll run quantized and full-precision runs to quantify quality tradeoffs.
[07:10] Amira Patel: Can we include an estimate of cost per 1k tokens at that latency target? Finance wants hard numbers for approvals.

[07:19] Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll model cost/k tokens for both hosted baseline (current config), hosted with caching/batching, and dedicated at three commit levels. We'll show marginal savings and break-even points.
[07:34] Marta Gonzalez: On observability, we'll give you a token-level breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and traces. The console supports alerting for token-volume and cost thresholds.
[07:46] Evan Chu: One more: data residency — some of our EU customers require logs retained within EU. How granular is your region-based retention?

[07:56] Marta Gonzalez: We can configure retention and region for logs; audit logs and payloads can be restricted to region for private deployments, and hosted has region-specific options — we'll include specifics in the security docs.

[08:10] Sofia Reyes: Ok, sounds like we have alignment on the big picture. Let's capture the pilot success criteria now: 1) p95 < 300ms for core route during peak, 2) <15% monthly cost uplift vs baseline, 3) smooth SSO/KMS integration and audit-ready reports. Is everyone comfortable with those?
[08:32] Evan Chu: Yes, those are reasonable.
[08:35] Amira Patel: Finance will add a 'max invoice delta' as a hard constraint — we'll send the number after this call.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick walkthrough of the A/B bench plan — Priya, can you summarize steps?

[09:05] Priya Nandy: Sure. Step 1: Redwood provides harness + sample data. Step 2: ParcelShift runs harness against hosted baseline and collects metrics. Step 3: Run with recommended batching + caching config. Step 4: Run against dedicated-like profile (simulated). Step 5: Share results and iterate. Expected wall time ~3-6 hours total for the harness runs depending on scale.
[09:34] Markus Huber: Will the harness produce cost estimates automatically or do we need to map tokens to invoices?

[09:41] Priya Nandy: It logs tokens and request metadata; we'll include a simple calculator that maps usage to the scenarios we'll send. So yes, it will give estimated invoice deltas under different price tiers.
[09:55] Jordan Lee: We're almost at the security bit — Marta, what docs exactly will you share?

[10:01] Marta Gonzalez: SOC 2 Type II report redacted, ISO cert references, KMS integration guide, IdP/SAML SSO guide, audit log schema, and our data retention policy. I'll attach a short summary email and the full deck.
[10:18] Sofia Reyes: Perfect. Also, can you include an architecture sketch of the hybrid routing suggestion? That's helpful for our infra review.
[10:27] Priya Nandy: We'll include a small diagram and a sample routing policy JSON.

[10:35] Evan Chu: Two nitpicks from our infra lead — first, we need deterministic cold start behavior for large models; second, can Redwood guarantee KV cache warmup strategies so early traffic doesn't suffer?

[10:48] Priya Nandy: We have cache pre-warming and persistent warm pools as an option for Dedicated. For hosted, prefix caching and sticky routing during rollout reduce cold starts. We'll document warmup recommendations for your traffic patterns.
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: If we go with sticky routing, how does that interact with autoscaling? We don't want overloaded nodes stuck with sticky sessions.
[11:15] Priya Nandy: Sticky routing is time-limited and works with autoscale policies; you can set session affinity TTLs that allow rebalancing if a node gets unhealthy.

[11:30] Jordan Lee: Alright, we're approaching the last segment. Quick recap: Jordan to send per-route token breakdown and pricing scenarios; Priya to deliver benchmark harness; Marta to send security materials; ParcelShift to provide prompts and constraints; Markus to check VPC peering. Any other blockers?
[11:51] Amira Patel: Please include a conservative invoice projection for a spike of +50% usage in the worst week — we want to ensure approvals cover that.
[12:00] Jordan Lee: Will do. We'll label it 'stress-case delta'.
[12:06] Sofia Reyes: One small ask — can Redwood include a short 'playbook' doc for our on-call to triage inference issues (first 3 steps) so our SREs don't call you for every blip?
[12:20] Marta Gonzalez: Yes — we have an on-call triage runbook template; we'll customize it for ParcelShift and attach it to the security/ops bundle.
[12:35] Jordan Lee: Great. Proposed dates: benchmark week of 6/16, SSO/KMS deep-dive 6/17, follow-up review 6/23 to finalize pilot commit. Does that align with your timeline?
[12:48] Evan Chu: Yes that works for engineering and product. Finance will aim to review the pricing by 6/18.
[12:55] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Any final questions?
[13:02] Markus Huber: Just to confirm the pilot length — 90 days?
[13:06] Jordan Lee: 90 days is standard; we can make it adjustable, but we'll model economics for 30/60/90 day pilots in the pricing doc.
[13:20] Sofia Reyes: Thanks everyone — appreciate the focus. We'll wait for the artifacts and set up the deep-dive invite.
[13:28] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with action items in the next 24 hours. Bye!
[52:00] Meeting ended
